q: By default, how does Playwright Test execute test files?
options: Sequentially in a single worker process
In parallel across multiple worker processes
Only when triggered via CI/CD pipelines
explain: Playwright Test runs test files in parallel by default to maximize execution speed, utilizing multiple worker processes based on available CPU cores.

q: You have 1 test file with 2 tests, 3 projects (chromium, firefox, webkit)  (6 tests in total) and fullyParallel=false. How many workers are used with --workers=2?
explain: With fullyParallel=false, tests in a file run together in one worker. 1 file x 3 projects gives 3 file-runs. With --workers=2, only 2 workers are needed and used, and the third file-run waits for a free worker.

q: You have 1 test file with 2 tests, 3 projects (chromium, firefox, webkit) (6 tests in total) and fullyParallel=false . How many workers are used with --workers=4?
explain: With fullyParallel=false, each file-run is one unit of work. 1 file x 3 projects gives 3 file-runs, so only 3 workers can be busy. The 4th worker is never used, even though --workers=4.
